acceptance_criteria.given: A user enters a URL that does not exist on the sandbox site
acceptance_criteria.then: They see a custom 404 page with a 'Page not found' heading and a helpful explanation instead of the framework default.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user is on the custom 404 page
acceptance_criteria.then: They are redirected to the site's root URL.
acceptance_criteria.when: They click the 'Return to Home' button

acceptance_criteria.given: The site is in dark mode
acceptance_criteria.then: The background and text colors match the established dark theme palette.

acceptance_criteria.given: A screen-reader user visits the 404 page
acceptance_criteria.then: The 'Page not found' h1 is the first meaningful element announced.

assumptions.assumption: The 'Return to Home' button should be the primary branded style (anz-blue).
The page should not include extra links like 'Contact Support' to maintain focus.

clarified_description: Implementation of a custom 404 error page for the Pixie sandbox site to replace the default framework error. The page will feature a professional, helpful tone, a centered 'hero' layout, and a single primary action button to return the user to the homepage. The page must be fully responsive, support both light and dark themes via the existing site theme state, and meet accessibility standards for keyboard and screen-reader users.

constraints.detail: Must use the existing Next.js routing and theme provider logic.

must: The page must display a clear 'Page not found' heading (h1).
The page must include a brief, helpful explanation of the error in plain language.
The page must provide a primary branded button that redirects the user to the homepage.
The page must automatically inherit the site's current light/dark theme state.
The page must be navigable via keyboard (tab order) and accessible to screen readers (semantic HTML).
The page must be wrapped in the site's existing layout (including Header and Footer).
outcome: Users who encounter a broken link are greeted with a branded, accessible error page that provides a clear path back to the homepage.
rationale: A custom 404 page is essential for maintaining professional brand perception. A centered hero layout with a single primary action (Return to Home) is the most efficient way to resolve a user's error state with minimal friction. By avoiding additional links and specialized error colors, we keep the page clean and prevent the error from feeling like a 'broken' part of the site.
should: The page should use a centered 'hero' layout to focus user attention.

criteria: Provides a clear 'Return to Home' button
user_stories.so_that: I understand what happened and can easily get back to the home page.
user_stories.want: A clear, branded error page when I type a wrong URL

jobs_to_be_done: Navigate back to functional parts of the site
users.name: Site Visitor
pain_points: Confusion caused by framework-default error pages
Feeling 'stuck' on a broken page with no navigation

children.text: Sorry, we couldn't find the page you're looking for. It might have been moved or deleted.

wont: Will not include additional links (e.g., Support or Contact) to minimize distraction.
Will not use 'error red' or other specialized error colors, sticking to the standard site palette.
